image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Horizontal stacked bar chart** (100% stacked/proportional bars)

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **stacking** within each horizontal bar to show three response categories.
- No faceting or small multiples.
- Categories are arranged as separate horizontal bars along the y-axis.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Issue/topic (e.g., Anxiety & depression, Bullying, Drug addiction, Drinking alcohol, Poverty, Teen pregnancy, Gangs) | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis; text labels at left |
| Response category (Major, Minor, Not) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue of stacked bar segments; column labels above segments |
| Percentage/value | Quantitative | Segment length/width along horizontal axis; numeric labels inside segments |

comments.raw_comment: This graph presents the major struggles an average high school student deals with daily. In my opinion, all the topics listed impact a teenager majorly. Each topic that is associated with a student can lead to trauma, use of drugs, or even death. I understand why anxiety and depression would be viewed as the most major because each topic listed below that, is an event that can end to a result of depression. For example, being in a gang is traumatizing and stressful. When teens get pregnant they completely break down, not knowing what decision to make next in the process. When a student is not as wealthy as their friends, money starts piling onto their daily lives, causing stress. Drinking and the use of drugs leads to changes in mood, lack of structure, and feeling lonely/useless. Lastly, bullying creates a sharp pain in a person leading them to be damaged for a long time due to how poor the student is getting treated. Notice how all the topics I just explained lead to anxiety and depression? These events pile onto a persons work load and once the load is to much they crash to the bottom which is the feeling of stress, loneliness, and sometimes, it can be emptiness. The bullying, gangs, pregnancies, etc become to much for a student to handle and they break down feeling completely useless. Luckily, I am happy and healthy. But, it hurts to look around my school to see the boy who's not accepted, the girl who overdosed on drugs, the girl who was kicked out of the house, etc.

As a high school student, I can relate.

comments.raw_comment:
I notice that anxiety and depression seem to be the biggest problem among teenagers. I would assume it's the pressure put on them by the school system, on top of everything else they deal with. That may not be the case, but that's what makes the most sense to me.

I also realize teen pregnancy seems to be pretty low on the chain, and that is probably due to the amount of time spent teaching children how big of an issue it is and how to prevent it.

Also, I believe that a lot of these issues could be tied to one another, leading from one issue into the next. Say someone is being bullied, given that it's the second biggest problem on this list. That bullying leads to depression. Depression could lead to substance abuse, such as drinking and doing drugs.

I feel like if we can do our best to help prevent and create solutions to some of these issues, it will create a domino effect that will help to decrease others as well.

comments.raw_comment: This graph shows what teens believe are the biggest issues teens face in our society. It shows just how big of a problem each one is with anxiety and depression at the top and gangs at the bottom. While I see this as an accurate prediction, I was quite surprised when I saw that drugs and alcohol weren't at the top of the list. Another concern that I had was that some of these problems cause one another, so a suspected raise in one could really just be an effect of another. For example, alcohol addiction in which only 45% believed it to be major could be the leading cause for 70% in anxiety and depression. But other than things like that, I agree with these statistics and can see all of these problems where I live. A catchy title could be "Teens Test The Truth," because we are the ones giving these statistics to the world. We are the ones that have to make these problems known, and we are the ones who have to end them.

Bullying can be separated into cyber, verbal, physical or racism because each has its own effects. I believe a catchy headline for this graph would be, "Bullying has Become a Major Teenage Problem."
